DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.433.topic: Baseline physical health checks before antipsychotics in children and young people
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.433.setting: West Midlands CAMHS consultants (survey of CAMHS consultant group)
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.433.standard: NICE guidelines on baseline physical and metabolic investigations before prescribing antipsychotics in children and young people with psychosis and schizophrenia

cycle1.result: Indications, record keeping and nutrition/activity assessment 100%; pulse and BP 88.9%; weight and height plotted 77.8%; movement disorder assessment always 44.4%; lipid profile always 44.4%; fasting glucose and HbA1c 33.3% yes, 66.7% never.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.433.other_findings: Recommended a physical/metabolic health check proforma and re-audit after its introduction. Data were collected by questionnaire of nine consultants.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.613.topic: Annual psychiatrist review of patients on depot antipsychotics
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.613.setting: General adult community mental health service, North Norfolk
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.613.standard: Maudsley prescribing guidelines: all patients on long-term antipsychotics seen by responsible psychiatrist at least once a year; target 100%

cycle1.result: 28/47 (approximately 60%) reviewed by a psychiatrist in the last year; 19 (approximately 40%) not reviewed.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.613.other_findings: Of the 19 not reviewed, only 8 had been offered an appointment. Findings discussed with the community team manager to arrange prompt reviews.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10688.standard: Recording of the 15 criteria of the Ligature Assessment Tool in ligature incident reports

cycle1.dates: Previous (third) audit, about two and a half years earlier
cycle1.result: 19% of reports recorded 11 or more criteria.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10688.intervention: No specific intervention (such as education or promotion) between the third and fourth cycles; the Ligature Assessment Tool had been introduced in 2020.

cycle2.result: 37% of reports recorded 11 or more criteria; 19 (35%) recorded all 15 criteria.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10688.other_findings: This was the fourth audit cycle since the tool was introduced in 2020. Plan to integrate the tool into the Trust incident reporting system.

PMID:21946877.setting: Auckland City Hospital, Orthopaedics and Older People's Health

cycle1.result: 24% had surgery within 24 hours of admission; of those not operated within 24 hours, 39% were awaiting theatre availability. Inpatient mortality 5%; median length of stay 27 days; 84% transferred to Older People's Health.

PMID:21946877.other_findings: Fast-tracked patients (n=43) had median length of stay 23 days vs 28 days with usual care. 35% were discharged to a higher level of care; 44% walked unaided before fracture but only 1% at discharge.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znab430.019.topic: Cholecystectomy after ERCP for bile duct stones
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znab430.019.setting: Single centre, Royal Victoria Infirmary, Newcastle upon Tyne
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znab430.019.standard: NICE CG188: bile duct clearance and cholecystectomy offered for bile duct calculi, or documented reason if declined

cycle1.result: 45/82 (55%) had a cholecystectomy after ERCP; of the 37 without cholecystectomy, 20 (54%) had no documented justification.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znab430.019.other_findings: Robust follow-up and documentation measures have since been put in place and a follow-up audit is under way.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.462.setting: Wolverhampton Older Adult Enhanced Community Mental Health Teams, Black Country Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.462.standard: BCHFT standard operating procedure: 15 standards for depot prescription writing

cycle1.result: Standard 3 (signed, dated, name printed) 75%; Standard 7 (interval using the word 'every') 19%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.462.intervention: Memory aid for prescribers placed at the front of depot card folders.

cycle2.result: 6 of 15 standards 100%; Standard 3 fell to 15%; Standard 7 improved to 31%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.462.other_findings: Standard 3 non-compliance was mainly due to no space for printing prescriber's name; depot cards to be revised to include signature and name columns.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keag121.310.setting: Single-centre biologic registry, The Royal Wolverhampton NHS Trust

cycle1.result: 78/191 (40.8%) met EULAR criteria for difficult-to-treat RA; erosive disease was the only multivariate predictor.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keag121.310.other_findings: Univariate associations included erosive disease, coexistent osteoarthritis and lack of concurrent csDMARD use.

DOI:10.1093/bjd/ljad113.352.setting: Phototherapy unit, Sandwell and West Birmingham Hospitals NHS Trust
DOI:10.1093/bjd/ljad113.352.standard: BAD phototherapy guidelines: urgent referrals to start treatment within 3 weeks of referral; local guidelines on documenting severity scores

cycle1.result: Time from referral to treatment start was 12 months; only 26% of referrals had documented disease severity scores.

DOI:10.1093/bjd/ljad113.352.other_findings: A pre-pandemic audit (March 2021) found a 6-week wait. 73% of urgent referrals were for eczema, 16% psoriasis.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.912.setting: Assertive Outreach Team, Sussex Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.912.standard: Trust guidance on HDAT monitoring (HDAT monitoring form plus physical health assessment)

cycle1.result: 4 patients on HDAT (117-150% BNF maximum); only one had an HDAT form, which was out of date. 39/52 (75%) had a physical health assessment in the past 12 months.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.912.other_findings: Barriers identified: lack of team awareness of HDAT, no reliable system to flag physical health checks and insufficient equipment.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10408.topic: Physical health monitoring on psychiatric wards
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10408.setting: Working-age general adult acute psychiatric inpatient ward
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10408.standard: Completion and timeliness of physical health checks (examination, observations, height/weight, ECG, bloods, cardiometabolic checklist)

cycle1.result: Physical examinations completed in 93%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10408.intervention: Daily MDT reviews, job list integration and master list; then a whiteboard with colour coding for task tracking, post-MDT reviews, staff reminders and induction sessions.

cycle2.result: Physical examinations 100%; physical observations maintained at 100%; reduced delays and more BMI measurements completed.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10408.other_findings: Barriers included gender-based refusal of ECGs and reluctance of patients with eating disorders to have BMI measured.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11751.topic: Follow-up after antidepressant initiation in young adults
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11751.standard: NICE: patients aged 18-25 reviewed within one week of antidepressant initiation or dose increase and again within four weeks

cycle1.result: 3/55 (5.5%) fully compliant; 4/55 (7.3%) reviewed within one week; 8/55 (14.5%) within four weeks.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11751.other_findings: 12 patients had no documented follow-up; most reviews were by telephone. Suggested automatic booking of a 1-week telephone review.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.417.topic: Folate and vitamin B12 testing and treatment
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.417.standard: BSH guidelines and NICE clinical summaries on diagnosis and treatment of folate and cobalamin deficiency; target 100% for all standards

cycle1.result: Standards 1, 2 and 5 were 100%; standards 3 and 6 (treatment per BNF) were 0%; standard 4 not applicable.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.417.intervention: Results shared with the MDT and an algorithm created and circulated.
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.417.other_findings: Re-audit sample was small, so a further cycle was suggested.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.256.topic: ECG on admission to psychiatric wards
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.256.setting: General adult inpatient wards, Clock View Hospital, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.256.standard: Mersey Care physical health policy: ECG within 24 hours of admission; NICE and RCP guidance

cycle1.result: 31/60 had an ECG within 24 hours; of the other 29, reason documented in 16. 13 abnormal ECGs, only 3 referred for further investigation.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.256.other_findings: No documentation of the ECG report in one third of cases. Recommended induction teaching and training ward nurses to perform ECGs.

DOI:10.1093/bjd/ljaf085.077.standard: NICE NG198: oral lymecycline with a topical agent for a maximum of 12 weeks then reassessment, avoiding concurrent oral and topical antibiotics

cycle1.result: 22% fully adherent; 54% received a topical treatment; 13% had concurrent oral and topical antibiotics; median continuous duration 4 months (range 1 month to 7.5 years).

DOI:10.1093/bjd/ljaf085.077.other_findings: Recommended clinician education, integrating NICE guidance into clinical systems and structured treatment reviews.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10605.topic: Physical health investigations on admission to psychiatric wards
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10605.setting: Nine general adult inpatient wards, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10605.standard: Trust physical health policy: admission blood tests and ECG within 24 hours

cycle1.result: FBC 89 (56%); U&E 90 (56%); LFT 93 (58%); TFT 90 (56%); HbA1c 83 (52%); lipids 89 (56%); ECG 86 (54%); urine pregnancy test 15/69 women (22%); urine drug screen 31 (19%).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10605.other_findings: Recommended induction teaching, nursing awareness of pregnancy testing and daily review of patients declining investigations.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.583.topic: VTE risk assessment in mental health inpatients
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.583.setting: 23 inpatient wards, Black Country Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.583.standard: NICE NG89: VTE risk assessment on admission or first consultant review, reassessment, and prophylaxis where indicated

cycle1.result: 30 (59.2%) risk assessed within 24 hours; 2% reassessed during admission; all 3 at-risk patients (6.1%) given prophylaxis but none reassessed for continued need.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.583.other_findings: Recommended VTE teaching at junior doctor induction and a Trust VTE policy including mental health risk factors.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znad348.161.topic: Time to ERCP for acute gallstone cholangitis
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znad348.161.setting: District general hospital, Princess Alexandra Hospital, Harlow
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znad348.161.standard: NICE: ERCP within 72 hours of diagnosis of acute gallstone cholangitis

cycle1.result: Median time to ERCP 10 days (5-24); moderate-severe 8 days (5-19), mild 28 days (9-46).

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znad348.161.intervention: Additional referral pathways to three nearby tertiary centres for ERCP; results presented to surgical MDT.

cycle2.result: Median time to ERCP 6 days (4-9); moderate-severe 6 days (6-8), mild 4 days (4-25).

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znad348.161.other_findings: 41 patients across both cycles. Median length of stay fell from 8 (6-13) to 7 days (4-10).

DOI:10.1136/emermed-2017-207308.24.topic: Resuscitation futility in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest
DOI:10.1136/emermed-2017-207308.24.setting: Emergency Department, Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh

cycle1.result: 202 (71.4%) low, 46 (16.3%) intermediate and 35 (12.4%) high risk of CPR futility by SPICT score.

DOI:10.1136/emermed-2017-207308.24.other_findings: 27.7% of low-risk patients survived to discharge vs 2.17% intermediate and 2.86% high risk; suggests community DNACPR implementation is suboptimal.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.100.setting: Approved Centre (acute psychiatric unit), Tallaght University Hospital
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.100.standard: Mental Health Commission rules governing the use of seclusion (13 rules)

cycle1.dates: Before introduction of the Integrated Care Pathway (2012)
cycle1.result: Compliance across the 13 MHC rules ranged from 3% to 100%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.100.intervention: Seclusion Integrated Care Pathway introduced in 2012 to record and monitor each seclusion episode.

cycle2.result: Compliance ranged from 69% to 100%; 100% compliance with five of the 13 rules.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.100.other_findings: Improvements in medical and nursing reviews, informing patients of reasons and likely duration of seclusion, and informing next of kin. An audit immediately after ICP introduction was also done.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.431.topic: Alcohol use disorder assessment on psychiatric admission
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.431.setting: Eight general adult inpatient wards, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.431.standard: Assessment and management of alcohol use disorders following admission (alcohol history, weekly quantity, CIWA-R, bloods, referral)

cycle1.result: Alcohol history documented 45%; weekly quantity 22%; CIWA-R on admission 0.7%; referral to community alcohol services 3%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.431.intervention: Recommendations from the original audit implemented (details not reported).

cycle2.result: Alcohol history documented 81%; weekly quantity 8%; CIWA-R 4.0%; referral to community alcohol services 7%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.431.other_findings: Gamma GT and magnesium checks on admission improved. Further recommendations: induction teaching, CIWA-R training and a ward flow chart.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11428.topic: Mental health risk assessment in paediatric emergency department
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11428.standard: NICE NG225: completion of ED mental health risk assessment tool and ED mental health form

cycle1.result: Risk assessment tool completed 7/59 (11.9%); ED mental health form opened 37/59 (62.7%); mental state examination completed 16/37 (43.2%); DPS score assigned 29/37 (78.4%).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11428.other_findings: The tool may be unsuitable for children (capacity rather than competence) and overlaps with the form. Plan to revise tools and add education.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.411.topic: PPI cover with SSRIs in older adults
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.411.setting: Older adult community mental health team
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.411.standard: Maudsley Guidelines: PPI prescribed if SSRIs cannot be avoided in patients at high bleeding risk

cycle1.result: 56.5% of patients on SSRIs prescribed a PPI.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.411.intervention: Results presented to prescribers within the team.

cycle2.result: 64.7% of patients on SSRIs prescribed a PPI.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.411.other_findings: Only 1 patient had bleeding risk explicitly documented. Many PPIs were started before the SSRI, possibly inflating results.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.294.topic: Mental Health Act medical recommendation quality
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.294.standard: Mental Health Act 1983 criteria for Section 2 and 3 medical recommendations, using the Mason et al. (2012) audit tool

cycle1.result: Mental disorder and nature/degree well documented; justification of risk to health, safety or others poorly documented, lowest for health.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.294.other_findings: Recommenders often did not identify which of the three risk categories applied. Results presented at teaching and inclusion in junior doctor induction recommended.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.457.topic: Baseline physical health checks before antipsychotic initiation
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.457.setting: Intensive Home Treatment Team, Bradford District Care NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.457.standard: BDCFT Antipsychotic Physical Health Monitoring Shared Care Guidelines

cycle1.result: 32% had a full physical health check before antipsychotic initiation; 56% incomplete; no individual investigation fully compliant; 40% had checks reviewed by a professional.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.457.other_findings: BMI/weight was least often completed and HbA1c was the least completed blood test.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11522.topic: Menstrual health screening on psychiatric wards
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11522.setting: Female inpatient psychiatric wards, Lambeth Hospital, South London and Maudsley
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11522.standard: Active screening for menstrual and menopausal health on admission

cycle1.result: 3/44 (7%) actively screened; 8/44 (18%) had appropriate menstrual health intervention.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11522.intervention: Staff training, patient information materials and updated clerking prompts.

cycle2.result: 28/45 (62%) actively screened; 33/45 (73%) had appropriate menstrual health intervention.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11522.other_findings: Menstrual symptoms were identified more consistently after the changes, leading to counselling, products and leaflets.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.297.setting: Mental health liaison service, Aneurin Bevan University Health Board acute hospitals
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.297.standard: RCPsych PLAN quality standards: 100% essential, 80% expected and 60% desirable standards met

cycle1.result: 30% of essential standards not met and 21% somewhat met; 36% of expected standards met, 41% not met; 89% of desirable standards not met.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.297.other_findings: Weak domains included policies, urgent care, governance, induction and teaching. A business case for a consultant-led MDT is being developed.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.320.setting: Older Persons Community Mental Health Team
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.320.standard: NICE guideline on antipsychotics for behavioural and psychological symptoms of dementia; local CAIR form

cycle1.result: CAIR form present in 73% of notes (37% the new shorter version); 63% of forms fully completed; 100% had assessment of causes, non-drug interventions first, target symptoms and review within 3 months.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.320.other_findings: Risk-benefit discussions were documented vaguely. Teaching held, leaflet to be provided, team to revert to original CAIR form and re-audit in 6 months.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.275.standard: 100% of digital handover records completed by doctors at end of shifts

cycle1.result: 5.36% of digital handovers completed.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.275.intervention: PDSA cycle August 2022 to January 2023: information sharing, teaching at changeover inductions, administrative help with shared drive access, and regular audit and feedback.

cycle2.result: 91.94% of digital handovers completed (88.71% in December 2022).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.275.other_findings: 35.00% in April 2022 and 25.81% in August 2022; access for outside locums remains a problem.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.540.topic: Admission checklist for borderline personality disorder
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.540.setting: Nine acute care wards, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.540.standard: Trust BPD admission checklist completed at admission

cycle1.result: 0/60 admissions had a completed BPD checklist.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.540.other_findings: 40% of admissions were out of hours, with more use of the MHA; 40% of ST doctors could not find the checklist. Training and re-audit in 6 months planned.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keaa109.002.topic: Glucocorticoid adherence in giant cell arteritis
DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keaa109.002.setting: Single rheumatology department, Nuffield Orthopaedic Centre, Oxford

cycle1.result: 22% (last 7 days) and 40% (last 6 months) were not following their original recommended steroid regimen.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keaa109.002.other_findings: Most non-adherence was due to medical advice; others were forgetting, fear of side effects or confusion about preparations.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae118.048.topic: Early onset colorectal cancer presentation and management
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae118.048.setting: Prospective multicentre cohort, 11 hospitals in extended Northwestern Switzerland

cycle1.result: 38 (10.8%) had early onset colorectal cancer; diagnostic delay 6.5 weeks longer than late onset; adjuvant chemotherapy 55.6% vs 28.6%.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znae118.048.other_findings: Rectal bleeding was the main symptom in both groups (60.5% vs 37.0%); more early onset patients received an ostomy.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10573.topic: Naloxone provision for patients on opioid substitution treatment
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10573.setting: CGL drug and alcohol service, East Sussex
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10573.standard: UK guidelines on clinical management of drug misuse and dependence: 100% of clients prescribed OST offered naloxone

cycle1.result: 65/748 (8.7%) did not have naloxone, all of whom (100%) had been offered it and declined; 60 had expired naloxone; 54 had naloxone given but not coded on the opiate report.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10573.other_findings: Most common reason for declining was no longer injecting and no contacts using opiates (57%); stigma was also cited.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.588.topic: Citalopram and escitalopram dosing and QTc in older adults
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.588.setting: Older adult community mental health services, Wolverhampton
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.588.standard: MHRA 2014 guidance: maximum citalopram 20 mg and escitalopram 10 mg daily in older adults

cycle1.result: One patient on citalopram above the recommended dose (30 mg); escitalopram within limits; QTc risk documented in 2 (11.8%); ECG review at initiation or adjustment in 1 patient.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.588.other_findings: 6 (35.3%) were on concurrent QTc-prolonging medication, all antipsychotics.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10642.setting: Enhanced Teams, Folly Hall Community Mental Health Team
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10642.standard: NICE NG181 and local standards: serum lithium every 3 months; renal, thyroid and calcium every 6 months; side effect monitoring; fully met 91-100%

cycle1.result: Lithium levels every 3 months 44.4%; renal function 94.4%; thyroid function 88.9%; calcium 61.1%; side effect monitoring 100%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10642.other_findings: No action taken for one patient with out-of-range lithium. Recommended reminders, a lithium registry, business meeting discussion and a lithium champion; re-audit planned.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11802.setting: Working-age adult inpatient wards, Farnham Road Hospital
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11802.standard: Trust guideline: GASS-C completed at 30 days after clozapine titration

cycle1.result: GASS-C completed at 30 days in 3/8 (37.5%).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11802.other_findings: Constipation documented in clinical notes in 6 (75%) and laxatives prescribed in 7 (87.5%). Embedding GASS-C into titration workflow proposed with re-audit.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.251.topic: Risk assessment documentation at psychiatric admission
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.251.setting: Two acute mental health wards (male and female)
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.251.standard: Documented risk assessment (risk to self, others, property) in junior doctor admission clerking

cycle1.result: 12/30 (40%) had a junior doctor risk assessment in the clerking; 14 (47%) had no mention of risk on admission.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.251.other_findings: Of 12 assessments all covered self-harm and violence, but only 1 absconding. Teaching and a risk assessment template introduced, with re-audit under way.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11757.topic: Staff knowledge of transgender patient care
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11757.setting: Kent and Medway Mental Health NHS Trust (survey of medical staff)

cycle1.result: 83.7% had cared for transgender patients; 58.1% not confident; 86% had no training; 79.1% unaware of guidelines or policies.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11757.other_findings: 60.5% were unaware of UK gender reassignment processes; staff requested training on pronouns and legal frameworks.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.102.setting: Eight acute adult inpatient wards, Nottingham Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.102.standard: NICE and local guidance on prolactin monitoring and management of hyperprolactinaemia

cycle1.result: 19 patients had no prolactin assay during admission; 44.4% of antipsychotic-naive patients had baseline prolactin; 9.1% with hyperprolactinaemia had symptoms assessed; 27.3% had actions taken.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10355.topic: Mental Health Act Section 5(2) form completion
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10355.setting: Large acute NHS hospital, adult and paediatric medicine
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10355.standard: Proforma of 12 criteria for correct completion of Section 5(2) forms

cycle1.result: 84% of criteria met (202/240); 100% legally valid; 70% identified risks; 55% correct status deletions; 55% contained abbreviations; 40% stated detention was needed to allow MHA assessment.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10355.other_findings: Hospital revising Section 5(2) guidance and preparing example templates; re-audit planned.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.410.topic: Physical health assessment in crisis home treatment teams
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.410.setting: South Cambridgeshire Crisis Resolution and Home Treatment Team, Cambridgeshire and Peterborough NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.410.standard: HTAS standards: physical health assessment and medical review for 100% of service users

cycle1.result: Physical health assessment criteria met in 70.12%; medical review criteria met in 94.80%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.410.other_findings: 1232 referrals screened to find 77 eligible service users.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10552.topic: Dementia diagnosis and treatment in memory services
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10552.setting: 15 memory services, Tees, Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10552.standard: NICE NG97 (2018) and TEWV Dementia Pathway: diagnostic work-up, subtype diagnosis, cholinesterase inhibitors/memantine and cognitive stimulation therapy

cycle1.result: Dementia subtype given in 100%; medication offered when indicated in 96% (10 of 15 services 100%).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10552.other_findings: Only 2 services offered cognitive stimulation therapy to all suitable patients; 10 teams scored below 40%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.552.setting: Specialist addictions service (three hubs), Humber Teaching NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.552.standard: Attendance at an addictions prescriber review within the last 3 months for patients on OST

cycle1.result: 170/343 (50%) attended a prescriber review in the last 3 months (Hub 1 55%, Hub 2 34%, Hub 3 65%).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.552.intervention: Quality improvement plan then enhanced plan: new appointment letter, text confirmation and reminder, keyworker reminder, prescriber call to persistent non-attenders, and medication safety review for non-attenders.
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.552.other_findings: After the enhanced plan in December 2018 attendance was 258/339 (76%) across all hubs; Hub 1 dipped to 51% in October 2018 after the first plan.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.585.setting: Inpatient services, Humber Teaching NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.585.standard: Trust seclusion policy based on the Mental Health Act Code of Practice (review content and timing: within first hour, then 4-hourly until MDT)

cycle1.result: Above 80%: timing of review, record keeping, plan for continuing seclusion, risk to self and others, mental state examination. Below 60%: prescribed medications, medication side effects and physical observations.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.585.other_findings: A seclusion medical review template was developed and teaching delivered; re-audit planned in 1 year.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10598.standard: Trust policy for drug screening on admission

cycle1.result: Documentation about drug screening in 23/40 (57.5%); test offered to 21/40 (52.5%); 15/21 (71.4%) completed; 5/8 positive results referred to substance misuse services.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10598.other_findings: Reasons for refusal (6, 28.6%) were not documented; re-audit planned after 3 months.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.576.setting: Eight general adult inpatient wards, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.576.standard: Mersey Care Nutrition and Hydration Policy: MUST within 72 hours of admission and Nutrition Screening Tool Care Plan completed

cycle1.result: 36 (90%) had MUST completed within 72 hours; 31 (79%) had every element of the care plan completed; 3/5 (60%) high-risk MUST patients fully compliant.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.576.other_findings: Described as a re-audit but earlier results are not given. Dietitian referrals were not made consistently.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afag197.036.topic: Follow-up after cervical spine fracture in older adults
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afag197.036.setting: Major Trauma Centre, Cork University Hospital
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afag197.036.standard: Outpatient neurosurgical appointments arranged for patients aged 65 and over with documented follow-up plans at discharge

cycle1.result: 28/38 (74%) eligible patients had appointments arranged; 26% without planned specialist review.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afag197.036.intervention: Findings presented to Neurosurgery; consultants' secretaries reviewed every discharge summary and booked outpatient appointments.
DOI:10.1093/ageing/afag197.036.other_findings: Initial cycle 57 patients, median LOS 13 days, in-hospital mortality 12%; re-audit 14 patients, median LOS 9 days, no deaths.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znad348.078.topic: NELA risk assessment in emergency laparotomy
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znad348.078.setting: Single centre, University Hospital Hairmyres, NHS Lanarkshire
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znad348.078.standard: NELA guidelines for risk assessment and documentation in emergency laparotomy

cycle1.result: About 21% of CEPOD booking forms had a recorded NELA score; NELA form or risk score missing in up to 97% of files and operation notes.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znad348.078.other_findings: Mortality was 21% for NELA score over 20%; 48% stayed longer than 10 days.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.591.standard: Local Trust policy and Resuscitation Council UK standards for resuscitation equipment and weekly checklists

cycle1.result: 7/10 locations did not meet standards (missing or expired adrenaline, suction, oxygen masks); 4/10 wards had not completed the weekly checklist; 70% of staff-completed checklists were incorrect.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.591.intervention: Updated, more detailed checklist, standardised procedure for ward managers, regular audits and extra Resuscitation team staffing.
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.591.other_findings: A re-audit was done and changes are being rolled out Trust-wide, but re-audit results are not reported.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10615.setting: Seclusion areas across Humber Teaching NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10615.standard: Defined checklist of seclusion room recommendations

cycle1.result: No audited area was 100% compliant; no rooms had a bed; problems with blind spots, bedding, lighting and heating.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10615.other_findings: Four wards had no dedicated seclusion room, and patients were secluded in general areas on three of them.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.570.topic: Physical health information on transfer to secure wards
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.570.standard: Complete physical health notes on transfer (consultation records, prior physical history, complete prescription with allergies)

cycle1.result: 7/12 patients transferred with complete physical health notes; no formal verbal or written physical health handover.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.570.other_findings: A proforma for preadmission meetings is being introduced from February 2024 with re-audit in February 2025.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11708.topic: ECG monitoring for patients on antipsychotics
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11708.setting: Acute Mental Health Inpatient Centre (5 wards), Belfast Health and Social Care Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11708.standard: Maudsley prescribing guidelines: ECG on admission and before discharge if antipsychotic regimen changed

cycle1.result: 0% had a discharge ECG; 7/34 (20.59%) had no ECG during admission; 17/34 (50%) did not have an ECG within 7 days of admission.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11708.other_findings: Teaching session and reminder posters arranged, with a PDSA approach planned.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.300.setting: Acute psychiatric inpatient unit, The Orchard
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.300.standard: Standards in the New Oxford Textbook of Psychiatry for components of the psychiatric history

cycle1.result: Only patient ID and presenting complaint in 100%; medical history 72%; forensic history 44%; social history 39%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.300.intervention: Clerking proforma created and distributed to junior doctors.

cycle2.result: ID, PC, HPC, psychiatric history and MSE 100%; forensic history 73% (p = 0.015); social history 78% (p = 0.018); premorbid personality 89% (p = 0.005); medical history 94%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.300.other_findings: Personal history (39% to 56%) and family history (39% to 61%) improved but not significantly.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.454.setting: 7 psychiatry wards, Essex Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.454.standard: 80% completion of ward review documentation questions considered satisfactory

cycle1.result: Most questions did not meet the 80% standard; 'Responsible clinician' completed in 23.3%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.454.intervention: Strategies to improve record keeping, including automation of some fields, junior doctor induction teaching and awareness posters.

cycle2.result: 9 questions satisfactory (at least 80%); 7 above 45%; 17 low; 'Responsible clinician' 99.5% after automation.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.454.other_findings: Effectiveness of non-automated strategies was limited; making fields mandatory or auto-complete worked best.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.569.topic: Physical health monitoring in eating disorder day care
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.569.setting: Adult Eating Disorder Service day-care, Surrey and Borders Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.569.standard: NICE guidelines and MEED guidance: weight, height, BMI, pulse, sitting/standing BP and temperature every attendance; bloods and ECG by BMI schedule

cycle1.result: Average day-care admission 5.5 months; other results not reported.

cycle2.result: 100% monitoring of BMI, weight, BP and pulse at admission and last assessment; temperature monitoring fell by 11.1%; ECG and bloods fell by 11.1% at all points; one patient lacked BMI, BP and pulse at midpoint.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.569.other_findings: Average admission fell to 3.5 months. Faulty thermometer and COVID-related difficulty accessing primary care affected monitoring.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.91.standard: Trust guidelines for management of vitamin D deficiency

cycle1.result: 89% had vitamin D checked during admission; 25% of those tested within 1 week of admission; 89% needing treatment were prescribed supplementation, 94% at correct dose and duration.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.91.other_findings: Only 25% of those tested had adequate levels; recommended vitamin D as a routine admission blood test.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10698.setting: Inpatient units, Leeds and York Partnership NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 28 reports of unavailable ECG machines; 490 minutes spent searching (median 10 minutes, longest 120); 4 ECGs not done; 46% missing and 54% faulty machines.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10698.intervention: Escalation to senior leadership and more ECG machines sourced during the audit period.
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10698.other_findings: Plan to develop instructional flowcharts for escalating faulty machines.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.310.setting: Inpatient wards, Lincolnshire Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.310.standard: Restraint practice: documentation, de-escalation, post-incident debrief and reflection, care planning

cycle1.result: 100% documentation of type and outcome of restraint; 20-30% of restraints without de-escalation, debrief or MDT reflection; 12% involved patients in post-incident reflection.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.310.intervention: PDSA 2021-2022: PMVA de-escalation training, sharing practice via MDT, monthly restrictive practice hub meetings and root cause analysis.

cycle2.result: Patient involvement in post-incident reflection increased by 60%; care planning and de-escalation improved by 10-15%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.310.other_findings: Restraints fell by 10-30% on eleven wards from 2020 to 2022.

cycle1.result: 21 international stroke registries identified; core minimum dataset for acute stroke care agreed.

DOI:10.1093/ageing/afac218.098.other_findings: Later phases address non-acute care datasets, PROMs and implementation.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10617.topic: VTE risk assessment in mental health inpatients
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10617.setting: 16 inpatient wards, Coventry and Warwickshire Partnership NHS Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10617.standard: NICE VTE in over-16s guideline: risk assessment on admission or by first consultant review, and reassessment at consultant review

cycle1.result: 153 (63%) had a signed and dated VTE assessment on admission; 154 (63%) within 24 hours; 242 (99%) had no reassessment at consultant review.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10617.other_findings: 13 (5%) assessments unsigned or undated; recommended induction teaching and making the VTE section a required field.

DOI:10.1136/emermed-2015-205372.46.topic: VTE prophylaxis in lower limb immobilisation
DOI:10.1136/emermed-2015-205372.46.setting: Emergency Department, Stockport NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1136/emermed-2015-205372.46.standard: NICE recommendation for VTE risk assessment in lower limb immobilisation, RCEM GEMNet guidance and local policy

cycle1.result: 20/62 (32%) had a documented VTE risk assessment; none received thromboprophylaxis per local policy.

DOI:10.1136/emermed-2015-205372.46.intervention: Pathway redesigned to GEMNet guidance, local education and launch, electronic discharge prompt/block and orthopaedic engagement.

cycle2.result: 54/58 (93.1%) had a documented risk assessment; 25/58 (43%) high risk and prescribed thromboprophylaxis.

DOI:10.1136/emermed-2015-205372.46.other_findings: 40% at baseline would have been eligible under GEMNet; no short-term complications on chart review.
